= Real fuzz compatibility fixture

This suite builds tiny targets with `roc build --fuzz` against the released
roc-fuzz 0.4.3 platform, pinned by its content-addressed URL. Its API and native
CLI were reviewed at release commit
`1abb6f0f76fc3ed6016cdf5da4e16e8ed1cfdfc4`; no downstream script or workflow runs.
The platform release asset's published SHA-256 is
`d9bae1e93e6e94f3fafb4040861402dbab90af247023461d8e5451db4a3ae0f2`.
Roc also verifies the bundle's content hash during normal provisioning.

`spec.json` is the ordinary schema-1 compatibility contract: clean fixed-seed
replay, a one-second clean libFuzzer smoke, and a fixed-seed deliberate failure
that must exit 77. Both stdout and exit status remain exact. Variable libFuzzer
statistics are explicitly ignored for comparison and retained as raw stderr.
The LLVM optimization mode remains controller-owned; fuzz builds use
`--opt=speed`, because the compiler rejects `--fuzz` with the ordinary dev backend.

`tests/run_fuzz_compatibility_smoke.py` supplies only the release asset transport
substitute used by the other compatibility smoke. The shared native utility
performs real archive admission, compiler checks, builds and executions. Separate
negative probes show that an unexpected 77 is incompatible, a crash message over
the existing output bound is `output-limit`, and an outer 200 ms deadline is
`test-timeout`, even with ignored stderr and a superficially matching expected
exit. The unbounded inner-run setting is used only under that outer deadline;
it never starts an unattended campaign.

The pinned platform ships Linux x64 musl and macOS arm64 inputs. This fixture
claims no Windows, Linux arm64, or Intel macOS coverage. A bounded clean run
establishes runner integration, not absence of bugs in the compiler or platform.

To run with the existing native runner and a real installed compiler:

[source,sh]
----
ROC_COMPATIBILITY_BINARY=/path/to/runner \
ROC_FUZZ_SMOKE_COMPILER=/path/to/roc \
ROC_FUZZ_SMOKE_EVIDENCE=/tmp/fuzz-smoke-evidence \
python3 tests/run_fuzz_compatibility_smoke.py
----

Use a fresh evidence directory for each invocation. It retains only the actual
host/compiler identity, command/result
JSON and raw diagnostic logs, never the temporary executables or package cache.
